breaks.quote: He tried out his opening line on his morning customers. Before December, he was confident.
breaks.why: The change from sending an assistant to being confident is given as an outcome with no steps between, so the reader has to guess how it happened.

breaks.quote: he came to me with a deadline: the December meeting, in his own voice.
breaks.why: The deadline is the only pressure, and nothing shows what Aiman stands to lose if he misses it, so the reader cannot feel why the beat matters.
The reader gets no step between the deadline and his confidence, so they must guess how he got from avoiding the boardroom to feeling ready.

breaks.quote: He tried out his opening line on his morning customers.
breaks.why: A staged action built from nothing the person said, which proves the point and which the reader has to take on trust.
A feeling stated as fact with no words from Aiman to earn it, so the reader cannot trust the case.
A short closing sentence carries the whole outcome as a new fact, so the reader gets the result without the steps that led to it.
